headword: {七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}き
gloss: fall seven times, get up eight; never give up

definitions.gloss: fall down seven times, get up eight
definitions.explanation: A proverb encouraging perseverance and resilience. No matter how many times you fail, you should always get back up and try again.

examples.japanese: {七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{精神|せいしん}→精神：03377_seishin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{頑張|がんば}ろう→頑張る：01222_ganbaru⟧。
examples.english: Let's persevere with the spirit of 'fall seven times, get up eight.'

examples.japanese: ⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦しても→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{諦|あきら}めない→諦める：01813_akirameru⟧。{七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}き⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Even if I fail, I won't give up. Fall seven times, get up eight.

examples.japanese: ⟦{人生|じんせい}→人生：03355_jinsei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}き。⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦でも→でも：noentry⟧⟦やり{直|なお}せる→やり直す：03172_yarinaosu⟧。
examples.english: Life is about getting back up no matter how many times you fall. You can always start over.

notes:
PROVERB MEANING:
Literally 'seven falls, eight rises.' The idea is that even if you fall seven times, you rise one more time than you fall, emphasizing resilience and perseverance.

CULTURAL NOTE:
This proverb reflects the Japanese cultural value of ⟦{頑張|がんば}り→頑張る：01222_ganbaru⟧ (perseverance, persistence). It encourages people not to be defeated by setbacks.

DARUMA CONNECTION:
The ⟦{達磨|だるま}→だるま：06539_daruma⟧ (Daruma doll) is a symbol of this proverb. Daruma dolls are weighted at the bottom so they always return to an upright position when tipped over.

- ⟦{諦|あきら}めるな→諦める：01813_akirameru⟧: Don't give up
- ⟦{根性|こんじょう}→根性：19215_konjou⟧: guts, determination
